what: DexCom makes continuous glucose monitors: small sensors worn on the body that read glucose levels every few minutes and send them to a phone, replacing finger-prick testing for people with diabetes.
customers: People with type 1 and type 2 diabetes, prescribed by doctors and paid for by insurers and health systems.
money: disposable sensors replaced every ten to fifteen days
moat: Sensors are consumable and replaced constantly, so each new patient produces recurring revenue, and insurer coverage and clinical data took years to establish.
risks: Abbott competes directly with its own sensor at a lower price point
US distribution changes caused a sales disruption that took time to recover from
Reimbursement decisions determine which patients qualify
It pays no dividend and trades at a high multiple
opportunities: Revenue grew about 16% last year and about 17% a year over three years
Return on invested capital of 25% with almost no debt
Type 2 diabetes patients not on insulin are a far larger market than its current base
watch: New patient starts and the rate of expansion into type 2 diabetes.
